title: Unify queue adapter for Redis/Kafka and perform consumer dependency upgrades
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Problem: Our async worker stack has grown organic patches over multiple quarters: separate shims for Redis Streams and Kafka, duplicated lease/prefetch logic, inconsistent retry semantics, and outdated client versions (redis-rs 0.27, rdkafka 0.29). This causes bugs when altering retry windows, makes reasoning about backpressure hard, and increases the cognitive overhead for on-call triage.

Goal: Replace the current dual-shim approach with a single, protocol-agnostic QueueAdapter interface and two thin protocol implementations. Standardize retry semantics to an idempotent-first policy with exponential backoff + decorrelated jitter and a configurable dead-letter policy. Upgrade Redis and Kafka client libraries to the community-supported 2026 LTS releases, and add end-to-end metrics and dashboards for prefetch, inflight counts, shed events, and retry histogram.

Non-goals: Rewriting the entire worker scheduler; changing business routing rules; introducing cross-tenant sharing for leases in this ticket. Those will be separate follow-ups if needed.
acceptance_criteria: New QueueAdapter trait implemented with two protocol drivers: redis_streams_driver and kafka_consumer_driver
All existing consumers compile and run against the unified adapter with feature-flagged rollout
Retry behavior unified: first attempt uses idempotent-safe fast path, subsequent attempts use exponential backoff with jitter configurable per route
Redis client upgraded to redis-rs v0.30+ and rdkafka upgraded to 0.31+ with no runtime regressions in CI
Observability: dashboards added for inflight_by_route, prefetch_holdoff, shed_events, retry_latency_histogram; alerts for sustained shed rate > 0.5% for 10m
No increase in 95th percentile processing latency beyond 10% on staging load tests; cost metrics documented
comments: 2026-02-20 Avery Chen: Filed initial ticket after a postmortem highlighted inconsistent retry jitter and duplicate lease code paths. Linked the incident: https://redwood.atlassian.net/incident/IR-2026-02-15

2026-02-23 Mateo Ruiz: Spike completed — created an experimental QueueAdapter trait and validated Redis Streams and Kafka drivers can share the prefetch + lease lifecycle. Prototype branch: github.com/redwood-inference/serving/compare/queue-adapter-spike
2026-02-28 Design review: Decided to keep per-protocol tuning knobs in drivers (max_prefetch, ack_batch_delay) but enforce a single public contract for retry and backpressure signals.
2026-03-03 Eng sync: Discovered rdkafka client bump requires rebasing our partition assignment logic; allocated a 2-day subtask for that. Created ENG-111223 for partition assignment refactor.
2026-03-05 Mateo Ruiz: Benchmarks on staging with 50K msgs/s showed ~8% improvement in throughput after removing duplicate prefetch bookkeeping. Added regression tests for consumer lease handoff.
2026-03-09 QA: Found an edge case where long-running handler tasks caused inflight accounting drift when a worker restarts quickly. Patch PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/4592

2026-03-11 Observability: Dashboard PR merged adding metrics: worker_prefetch_count, worker_inflight_by_route, worker_shed_events_total, worker_retry_latency_ms. Link: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/async/queue-health

2026-03-12 Mateo Ruiz: Rollout plan drafted — start with feature-flagged driver on a small fleet (10% of consumers) for 72h, monitor shed rate and p95 latency, then expand to 100% if stable. Blocker: upgrade needs S3 artifact rebuild on Dedicated infra (ticket ENG-111224).
notes: Trade-offs: Keeping protocol-specific knobs means we won't force identical behavior across Redis/Kafka (acceptable for 1.0), but simplifies the public contract for business code.
Security: Upgrading clients triggered a dependency scan; no high CVEs found but slsa provenance needs verifying for rdkafka binaries. Follow-up with security team required.
